newsitem.title: POLAND: BIG TO UP GDANSKI STAKE FEB 21- PAPER.
newsitem.headline: BIG TO UP GDANSKI STAKE FEB 21- PAPER.

text.p: Polish bank BIG SA will up its stake in Bank Gdanski to around 63 percent from the current 31.2 percent on February 21, the daily Rzeczpospolita reported on Tuesday quoting unofficial sources.
No one at the two banks or the finance ministry would comment on the article.
BIG, which holds its Gdanski shares directly and through two subsidiaries, is the only bidder for the treasury's offer of another 31.9 percent stake, or 6,260,240 shares, in Gdanski.
Last week BIG, whose full name is Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych SA, received the permission of the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, to hold between 50 and 66 percent of Gdanski.
Rzeczpospolita said BIG would pay 40 zlotys per share to up its stake. Gdanski closed on the bourse on Monday at 44 zlotys.
The Bank of New York as a depositary bank currently holds 19.5 percent of Gdanski's shares, represented by 19.5 percent of the bank's GDRs held by foreign investors.
Small investors on the Warsaw bourse hold the remaining shares. The treasury plans to hold on to about five percent of Gdanski shares.
